tests: a structural mutation leaves the tree's layout stale
a child added to a laid-out row reflows the whole row
removing a child closes the gap it left
a reparented child is re-boxed by its new parent, not its old one
reordering children re-solves the row in the new order
rationale:
Makes View's structural mutators move the tree layout generation. add_child, remove_child and move_child_to_index all left tree_layout_generation_ untouched, and both layout gates -- View::layout_children_if_needed and WidgetBridge::ensure_layout -- elide the pass while that counter matches the applied one. A structural mutation was therefore invisible to both gates and the pass was skipped, so the next frame painted the previous child set's solve: a new child got no box, the survivors of a removal kept the slots the old child set had been solved into, and a reparented child kept the box its former parent gave it.

publish_structure_change() now moves the layout generation, covering removal, reordering and the realm-reset paths; add_child_transactional does not route through it on success and moves the generation itself. add_child deliberately does not publish a structure change -- structure_generation_ invalidates a cached "is this view still under root" lookup, and an add can never detach a cached view -- so routing it through the shared helper would have defeated an O(1) bridge path.

The touched file is in render-assets-and-backends only because View lives under core/view. Nothing about what the view layer exposes changes: no public API, no new capability, no removed one. The pass this restores is one the iOS and web hosts already run unconditionally every frame; the gate is a macOS-only optimisation that was eliding a pass it should not have.

Five Catch2 cases cover add, remove, reparent and reorder plus the generation itself; each was negative-controlled with tools/scripts/confirm_failure.sh, and both halves of the fix were confirmed independently load-bearing.
